_note: An archetype attaches to an APPLICATION, not to a project. A product with a client portal and an admin console has two, and they are different shapes with different screens. This file says what shape an application is; industries.json says how it should look and speak; audiences.json sets the floors it may not go below. Colour and tone are deliberately absent here — three axes all asserting colour would conflict, and that argument belongs to the sector.

crm.label: Customer relationship management
crm.primaryObject: the relationship — a contact, an account or a deal, depending on what the business sells

coreScreens.purpose: what happened and when, in time order
a new record with the minimum fields

crm.navigationShape: list to detail, with the pipeline as a second view of the same set. The activity timeline lives inside detail and is the screen people actually read.
crm.density: dense: this audience lives in it and scanning many records at once is the job

antiPatterns.what: a detail screen that opens in a modal
antiPatterns.why: the record is the work, and a modal cannot be deep-linked, kept open, or compared against another

antiPatterns.what: requiring every field at creation
antiPatterns.why: a record captured late is a record lost; creation takes what is known now

erp.label: Enterprise resource planning, or any module of one
erp.primaryObject: the transactional document — an order, an invoice, a movement

coreScreens.purpose: one document, its lines, its state

erp.navigationShape: documents move through states, and the state is the primary filter everywhere. Master data is a separate area, not a tab of the transaction.
erp.density: very dense: tabular figures, many columns, and the row is the unit of work

antiPatterns.what: hiding the document state behind a colour
antiPatterns.why: state drives every downstream permission and it has to be readable as text

antiPatterns.what: a wizard for a document users create fifty times a day
antiPatterns.why: a wizard is for a first time, and there is no first time here

hrm.label: Human resources management
hrm.primaryObject: the person, and the events attached to them

coreScreens.purpose: one person, their record and their history
leave, expenses, changes — raised and tracked
what a manager owes an answer on

hrm.navigationShape: two audiences in one application: the employee sees their own record and their own requests, the manager sees a queue. The same screen serves both with different scope, and getting that scope wrong is the sector's signature defect.
hrm.density: moderate: read more often than edited, and by people who are not in it daily

antiPatterns.what: one navigation for employee and manager
antiPatterns.why: a manager's queue on an employee's home screen is a permission leak that looks like a layout choice

antiPatterns.what: salary visible in a directory
antiPatterns.why: the directory is the most-opened screen and the least-restricted one

portal.label: Client or customer portal
portal.primaryObject: the client's own holdings — whatever the business holds on their behalf

coreScreens.purpose: everything at a glance, the number that matters first
the list of what they have
one item, its history and its documents
what the business has told them

portal.navigationShape: overview leads, and everything else is a drill-down from it. The client sees only their own data and the boundary is absolute — a portal that leaks between clients has no second chance.
portal.density: moderate: read occasionally, by people who are not professionals in this domain

antiPatterns.what: presenting a figure without saying when it was valued
antiPatterns.why: an undated number is a claim the business cannot stand behind

antiPatterns.what: blending currencies into one total
antiPatterns.why: unless conversion is a stated feature, two currencies are two totals

antiPatterns.what: an empty state that only says 'no data'
antiPatterns.why: a new client's first screen is the empty state, and it is the whole first impression

admin-console.label: Internal administration console
admin-console.primaryObject: every other object in the system, from the operator's side

coreScreens.purpose: create and change, with validation visible
many at once, with a dry run

admin-console.navigationShape: one section per entity, flat and predictable. The operator learns the pattern once and applies it everywhere, so consistency between entities outranks optimising any single one.
admin-console.density: dense: this is somebody's whole working day

antiPatterns.what: designing the admin last, from whatever the client screens left over
antiPatterns.why: the admin is half the system and the half that gets used every day

antiPatterns.what: destructive actions with the same weight as ordinary ones
antiPatterns.why: an operator deleting a client at speed is the incident this screen exists to prevent

antiPatterns.what: an import with no dry run
antiPatterns.why: a bad import is discovered by the people whose data it corrupted

dashboard.label: Analytics or monitoring dashboard

coreScreens.purpose: the headline measures, current against a comparison
one measure, split by a dimension

dashboard.navigationShape: overview to breakdown to the underlying rows. Every figure must be traceable to the records that produced it, or the dashboard is decoration.
dashboard.density: dense, but a dashboard nobody can read at a glance has failed at its only job

antiPatterns.what: a number with no comparison
antiPatterns.why: 42 means nothing without last month, target, or both

antiPatterns.what: a chart type chosen for variety
antiPatterns.why: the form follows the question, and a pie chart answers almost none of them

antiPatterns.what: no stated freshness
antiPatterns.why: a stale dashboard is worse than no dashboard because it is acted on

marketplace.label: Two-sided marketplace or catalogue commerce

coreScreens.purpose: one item, everything needed to decide
the commitment, in as few steps as it can honestly take
what was bought and where it is
the other side of the market

marketplace.navigationShape: browse to listing to basket to checkout, and every step is a place people leave. Search is a first-class surface, not a header icon.
marketplace.density: moderate: the listing carries the decision and crowding it costs conversion

antiPatterns.what: cost revealed at the last step
antiPatterns.why: it is the single largest cause of abandonment and it is a design decision, not a pricing one

antiPatterns.what: requiring an account before checkout
antiPatterns.why: the account serves the business, and asking for it before the sale trades revenue for a record

booking.label: Scheduling and reservation
booking.primaryObject: the reservation, against a resource and a time

coreScreens.purpose: what was booked, and how to change it
what is coming, what has passed
the other side: capacity and rules

booking.navigationShape: availability first and everything else follows from it. Time zone is part of every screen or it is a bug waiting for a customer in another country.
booking.density: moderate; the availability view is the exception and can be dense

antiPatterns.what: showing times without a zone
antiPatterns.why: the first cross-border booking exposes it and the cost is a missed appointment

antiPatterns.what: cancellation buried in a policy page
antiPatterns.why: it is the second most-used flow and hiding it produces support calls, not retention

workflow-approval.label: Review and approval workflow
workflow-approval.primaryObject: the case, and the state it is in

coreScreens.purpose: what is waiting on me, oldest or most urgent first
everything needed to decide, on one screen
approve, reject, or return with a reason

workflow-approval.navigationShape: queue to case to decision and back to the queue. The loop is the product, and any step that breaks the return to the queue costs the reviewer their place.
workflow-approval.density: dense on the queue, focused on the case

antiPatterns.what: a decision with no reason field on rejection
antiPatterns.why: the person receiving it cannot act, and the next reviewer cannot learn

antiPatterns.what: losing queue position after a decision
antiPatterns.why: a reviewer working a hundred cases restarts their scan every time

content-site.label: Content, marketing or publishing site
content-site.primaryObject: the page, and the action it exists to produce
content-site.navigationShape: shallow and scannable. Most visitors arrive from search on a deep page, so every page is a landing page.
content-site.density: sparse: reading is the task and measure line length rather than eyeballing it

antiPatterns.what: an interstitial before the content
antiPatterns.why: the visitor came for the content and the interstitial is the business talking over them

antiPatterns.what: designing only the home page
antiPatterns.why: most arrivals never see it
